text: Lesson 44 asked whether a problem is new or has always existed. Query Store answers that with evidence -- its Regressed Queries report surfaces queries whose duration, CPU, or reads got meaningfully worse recently.

The same Plan Summary chart, read differently. Here it's annotated before and after a new index -- duration dropping from roughly 17-20 million microseconds down to 8-12 million once the index landed. If it doesn't drop, the fix didn't work.

Compare Plans lays two plan IDs for the same query top and bottom. A Clustered Index Scan at 51% cost in the older plan gets replaced by an Index Seek at 24% in the newer one -- the exact seek-versus-scan distinction, shown as the literal cause of a regression.

sp_query_store_force_plan locks the optimizer onto a known-good plan ID without touching the query. It's a stabilizer, not a permanent fix -- it buys time while you diagnose the real cause, then you unforce it once a real fix is in place.

Regression detection, before/after confirmation, side-by-side comparison, and forcing a fix -- the full Query Store workflow. Next up: blocking, locking, and deadlocks -- three genuinely distinct concepts that get confused constantly.
